question.leadin: Revolts against this policy ultimately led to 69 deaths in the Sharpeville Massacre.
question.text: Name this system of racial segregation in South Africa, which was opposed by the African National Congress. High school students protested against this system in the Soweto uprisings.
question.clue: Hendrik Verwoerd was a noted proponent of this policy, which was opposed by the African National Congress and which led to events like the Sharpeville massacre and the Soweto uprising.

swap.text: The Jameson Raid was an attempt to take over this largest city in South Africa.
swap.clue: Mandela posed as a farm worker at Liliesleaf Farm, located in this city, which was eventually raided leading to his capture and trial. The Soweto uprising occurred in this city, the largest in its country, after the introduction of Afrikaans.

question.text: In this nation that is plagued by hyperinflation, Morgan Tsvangirai and Robert Mugabe reached a power sharing deal in 2008 after allegations of election fraud.
question.clue: This country's first president was Canaan Banana, who was arrested in 1997 on charges of sodomy.

swap.leadin: European colonizing forces built a pair of modern African capital cities as far inland on this river as ships could sail from the Atlantic.
swap.text: Name this African river that is shorter than the Nile and longer than the Niger. A pair of neighboring central African countries share the name of this river; one styles itself a Republic and the other a Democratic Republic.
swap.clue: By 1740, Kazembe migrants conquered this river's upper salt pans for the Lunda Empire, which claimed Luba origins.

question.text: This Emperor of Ethiopia was overthrown during the Italian occupation. Despite a moving address to the League of Nations, he was forced to remain in exile until the end of World War II.
question.clue: From 1936 to 1941, this leader lived outside of his country because it was occupied by Italy during what became known as the Abyssinia Crisis.

swap.leadin: Charli XCX's Gujarati family moved to England after being expelled by this dictator along with thousands of other South Asians in 1972.
swap.text: Name this Ugandan dictator who overthrew Milton Obote, but was later toppled by Tanzanian forces in 1978.
swap.clue: This man expelled 50,000 Asians with British passports from his country.

question.text: Prince Johnson suggested that this country's president Charles Taylor had ordered the overthrow of Sankara. Taylor himself came to power after overthrowing this country's leader Samuel Doe.
question.clue: Perhaps its most controversial leader declared his "national unification policy" and announced an "open door policy," constructing the largest mercantile fleet in the world.

swap.text: A president of this country, Abdirashid Shermarke, was assassinated by a bodyguard, leading to the takeover of Siad Barre, who led this country's invasion of nearby Ethiopia in the Ogaden War.
swap.answerHtml: Somalia [or Federal Republic of Somalia; or Jamhuuriyadda Federaalka Soomaaliya]
swap.clue: After the dictator Siad Barre was ousted from power in this nation, warlords began to take control of autonomous regions such as Puntland.

question.leadin: This country is the second-largest oil producing country in sub-Saharan Africa. 10 points each.
question.text: Name this country, the largest in Africa that uses Portuguese as an official language.
question.clue: The Alvor Agreement was signed by this country's first president, Agostinho Neto.

swap.text: De Gaulle was called out of retirement to lead the Fifth Republic in part to help resolve the war led by the National Liberation Front against French occupation of this area.
swap.clue: A nuclear test named "blue jerboa" was carried out near this colony's town of Reggane.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about an African kingdom.
question.text: This Islamic kingdom, made up of Mandinka people, ruled in western during the 13th and 14th centuries from its capital at .
question.clue: It met its end nearly a century and a half later under the rule of Issihak II, when Judar Pasha led Moroccan forces to victory at the Battle of Tondibi.

swap.text: This President of Liberia from 1980 to 1990 was a supporter of American Cold War policies. In 1990, he was captured by rebel Prince Johnson, who was taped sipping a beer as this man was brutally tortured and then killed.

question.text: This city, whose name means "city of a thousand" is the capital of Madagascar.
question.clue: One woman who ruled from this city applied a trial by ordeal involving eating toxic tangena nuts en masse.

swap.leadin: This conflict was sparked by the death of Hamad bin Thuwaini and the HMS Glasgow was sunk during an operation in this war.
swap.text: Name this war that lasted about 45 minutes and is sometimes considered to be the shortest war in history.
swap.clue: The initial cause of the war was the death of Hamad bin Thuwaini, which led to a coup by Khalid bin Bargash, who seized the "House of Wonders" or Beit al-Ajaib - a palace located in modern-day Stone Town.

question.leadin: Answer these questions about European diplomacy in the first decade of the 20th century FTPE.
question.text: This 1906 conference confirmed the independence of Morocco and gave France the authority to control Morocco's Algerian border.
question.clue: The First Moroccan Crisis between France at Germany was defused at this 1906 conference. Britain honored the Entente Cordiale here by backing the French side completely.

swap.leadin: Name some stuff about African migrations.
swap.text: Shaka Zulu's invention of the spear known as the iklwa contributed to this period of chaotic warfare and migration in southern Africa, whose name means "crushing" in Zulu.
swap.clue: This period saw Moshoeshoe I unify his people to form a kingdom which now has its capital at Maseru.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the medical history of colonial-era Africa.
question.text: This colony's health system was generally regarded as the best in colonial Africa, with thousands of hospital beds in cities such as Stanleyville. This colony replaced a brutal "Free State" run by Leopold II.
question.clue: A jailed prophet lent his name to one rebellious group in this polity, the Kimbanguist church, which found a military arm in the ABAKO movement led by Joseph Kasa-Vubu.

swap.leadin: Brendan Koerner's book The Skies Belong to Us recounts George Wright hijacking a plane to this city, where Nina Simone attended a landmark 1969 cultural festival.
swap.text: Name this so-called "capital of the Third World," which sheltered fugitives like Donald L. Cox. A motel named for this city was the site of police killings during the 1967 Detroit riots.
swap.answerHtml: Algiers [or al-Jazā’ir; or Alger; accept Algiers Motel] (Algiers hosted the first Pan-African Cultural Festival.)
swap.clue: A leader of this city struck the diplomat Pierre Deval with a fly-whisk, initiating the series of events leading to French conquest in 1830.

question.leadin: This author of the memoir Unbowed was the subject of an Amnesty International letter-writing campaign after she was attacked and arrested while planting trees in the Karura Forest.
question.text: Name this woman who won the Nobel for establishing the Green Belt movement in Kenya, which supports the establishment of tree nurseries.
question.clue: This Kenyan Woman who won the Nobel Peace Prize for her work as the founder of the Green Belt Movement.

swap.leadin: This state was led by the Walashma dynasty like its predecessor, the Ifat sultanate.
swap.text: Identify this sultanate located on the western shores of the Gulf of Aden. Its general Ahmad Ibrahim al-Ghazi led several successful campaigns against Ethiopia and killed Emperor Dawit II.
swap.clue: This sultanate that fortified its "holy city" of Harar after Lebna Dengel allied Ethiopia with Portugal to fight its Afar and Somali forces. It was based north of the Ajuran Empire.
